DELIVERABLE — Corrected HUD prevalence-ceiling entry for the legacy HDE checklist, under 21 CFR Part 814 as in force on 2026-11-21. Draft for review by a qualified regulatory reviewer/clinician; not a regulatory determination and not device-specific advice.

=====================================================================
1. BOTTOM LINE / CORRECTION INSTRUCTION
=====================================================================
The legacy figure of 4,000 individuals per year is superseded. The checklist must use an annual ceiling of 8,000 individuals in the United States per year, taken from the definition of HUD in 21 CFR 814.3(n).

- Value to insert: 8,000
- Unit: individuals in the United States per year (an annual count of persons in the US population — not a percentage, not a rate per 100,000, not a device count)
- Comparator: "not more than 8,000" (inclusive; exactly 8,000 meets the definition). Do NOT write "fewer than 8,000" or "< 8,000".
- Governing citation: 21 CFR 814.3(n), Part 814, Chapter I, Title 21, as in force on 2026-11-21.
- Corroborating provision for diagnostic devices: 21 CFR 814.104(b) (subpart H), "not more than 8,000 patients per year".

=====================================================================
2. OPERATIVE TEXT (VERBATIM) AND SOURCE RECORD
=====================================================================
Primary source — 21 CFR 814.3(n), eCFR current:
URL: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/part-814/section-814.3 (fetched 2026-11-23T21:18:51Z; sha256 a92b8b1d4ba3; 5,326 characters)
Verbatim: "(n) HUD (humanitarian use device) means a medical device intended to benefit patients in the treatment or diagnosis of a disease or condition that affects or is manifested in not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year."

Corroborating fetches of the same operative text:
(a) https://ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-H/part-814 (fetched 2026-11-23T21:18:52Z; sha256 7c4288803759) — 814.3(n) identical.
(b) https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/part-814/subpart-A (fetched 2026-11-23T21:18:52Z; sha256 4ae5465fbc65; 15,209 characters) — 814.3(n) identical.
(c) https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title21-vol8/xml/CFR-2025-title21-vol8-part814.xml (fetched 2026-11-23T21:18:51Z; sha256 0aa9c4d303d5) — annual CFR edition 2025, 814.3(n) identical. This is the printed annual edition; it fixes the text in a non-drifting source.
(d) https://www.fda.gov/media/99933/download (fetched 2026-11-23T21:18:52Z; sha256 5a721ccc4086; 27 pages, 9,113 characters) — FDA slide deck, which states "A Humanitarian Use Device (HUD) is a medical device intended to benefit patients in treatment or diagnosis of a disease or condition that affects or is manifested in not more than 8,000 individuals per year in the United States" and prints the paragraph cite "21 CFR 814.3(n)" on the same slide.

Related provisions in the same subpart that carry the same 8,000 ceiling (for the consistency sweep in section 6):
- 814.100(b): "...diseases or conditions that affect or are manifested in not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year." (https://ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-H/part-814, sha256 7c4288803759)

Paragraph numbering within 814.102 to be confirmed against the eCFR table of contents at sign-off; the quoted text is verbatim.
- 814.104(b) (original applications, diagnostic documentation): "If the device is for diagnostic purposes, the documentation must demonstrate that not more than 8,000 patients per year would be subjected to diagnosis by the device in the United States." (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-H/part-814/subpart-H?toc=1, sha256 9511bc8faee9)
- Periodic-report provision, subpart H (814.126, paragraph number to be confirmed): "...if the number shipped or sold exceeds 8,000, an explanation and estimate of the number of devices used per patient..." — NOTE: this 8,000 is a DEVICE count trigger, not the patient ceiling. Do not let the checklist merge the two.

=====================================================================
3. POINT-IN-TIME VERIFICATION FOR "AS IN FORCE ON 2026-11-21"
=====================================================================
Two independent source types agree on 8,000: (i) the eCFR current text, fetched 2026-11-23T21:18:51Z (two days after the target date), and (ii) the 2025 annual CFR edition on govinfo (CFR-2025-title21-vol8). Because the current text on 2026-11-23 still reads 8,000, no amendment altering the 814.3(n) figure took effect on or before 2026-11-23, and therefore none took effect on or before 2026-11-21. The 2025 annual edition matches, so the figure has been stable from the 2025 edition through the fetch date.

Residual verification step to record in the checklist's change-control block before sign-off (not a blocker for the value): if the reviewing office requires a strict single-date snapshot rather than the current-plus-annual-edition pairing, pull the eCFR point-in-time view for 2026-11-21 (https://www.ecfr.gov/on/2026-11-21/title-21/part-814/section-814.3) and file the PDF alongside this record. Expected result: identical text.

Amendment history of 814.3 itself is not displayed in the fetched passages; do not write an amendment history line into the checklist without a separate Federal Register check. In particular, the commonly repeated explanation that the 4,000-to-8,000 change came from the 21st Century Cures Act is NOT established by any page in this record and must not be stated as fact in the checklist until verified against the statute and the Federal Register.

=====================================================================
4. WHAT THE PROOF-OF-ABSENCE SEARCH ESTABLISHES
=====================================================================
The harness searched the full text of the 814.3 eCFR page (5,326 characters), the subpart A page (15,209 characters) and the FDA slide deck (9,113 characters) for the strings "4,000 individuals per year", "4,000 individuals in the United States per year", "fewer than 4,000 individuals in the United States per year", "no more than 4,000 individuals in the United States per year", "prevalence of the disease or condition", "HUD ceiling" and "humanitarian use device definition". None of these strings occurs on any of the three pages.

This establishes that the 4,000 figure and the phrase "prevalence of the disease or condition" are not in the current regulatory text — it supports the strike of the legacy number. It does NOT establish that the pages are silent on the ceiling: all of them state 8,000 individuals in the United States per year. The value is therefore answered, not unstated.

=====================================================================
5. THE EDIT TO MAKE (STRIKE / INSERT)
=====================================================================
5.1 Strike the legacy line wherever it appears (item text, footnote, or appendix):
"HUD eligibility: the device must be intended to treat or diagnose a disease or condition affecting fewer than 4,000 individuals in the United States per year (21 CFR 814.3(n))."

5.2 Insert in its place:
"HUD eligibility: the device must be intended to benefit patients in the treatment or diagnosis of a disease or condition that affects or is manifested in not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year (21 CFR 814.3(n), as in force on 2026-11-21). The ceiling is inclusive: a disease or condition affecting or manifested in exactly 8,000 individuals per year meets the definition. For a device intended for diagnosis, the corresponding documentation requirement is that not more than 8,000 patients per year would be subjected to diagnosis by the device in the United States (21 CFR 814.104(b), subpart H)."

5.3 Three mechanical fixes that must accompany the number change:
(i) Comparator: replace any "fewer than", "less than" or "<" with "not more than" — the regulation is inclusive at 8,000.
(ii) Noun and unit: the definition counts individuals (persons) in the United States per year, not devices, not procedures, and not a percentage. If the checklist has a separate line for the 8,000-device shipped/sold reporting trigger in the periodic-report provision, label it "devices", not "individuals".
(iii) Citation: cite 814.3(n), not 814.3 generally and not subpart H generally. 814.3(m) defines HDE and is a different term; do not cite it for the ceiling.

5.4 Change-control entry to append:
"Item [x] corrected: HUD annual population ceiling changed from 4,000 to 8,000 individuals in the United States per year; citation confirmed as 21 CFR 814.3(n). Verified against eCFR (sha256 a92b8b1d4ba3, fetched 2026-11-23T21:18:51Z), eCFR part-level and subpart A pages (sha256 7c4288803759, 4ae5465fbc65), govinfo CFR-2025-title21-vol8 (sha256 0aa9c4d303d5) and FDA HUD slide deck (sha256 5a721ccc4086). Comparator changed to 'not more than'. Reviewer: ______ Date: ______"

=====================================================================
6. CONSISTENCY SWEEP — OTHER FIGURES IN PART 814 THE CHECKLIST MAY QUOTE
=====================================================================
Review each row and confirm the checklist is internally consistent with it. All 8,000 figures below are ceilings or triggers on different quantities; only row 1 is the HUD definition.
| # | Provision | Figure and unit | Quantity counted |
| 1 | 814.3(n) — HUD definition | 8,000 individuals in the United States per year (ceiling, inclusive) | Individuals with the disease/condition |
| 2 | 814.100(b) — purpose of section 520(m) | 8,000 individuals in the United States per year | Individuals with the disease/condition |
| 3 | 814.102 — designation review, criterion (i) | 8,000 people in the United States per year | Individuals with the disease/condition |
| 4 | 814.102 — designation review, criterion (ii) | 8,000 patients in the United States per year | Patients subjected to diagnosis (diagnostic devices) |
| 5 | 814.104(b) — diagnostic documentation | 8,000 patients per year in the United States | Patients subjected to diagnosis |
| 6 | Subpart H periodic-report provision (814.126; paragraph to confirm) | 8,000 devices shipped or sold | Devices — a reporting trigger, NOT a patient ceiling |
| 7 | 814.104(b)(5) — HDE cost provision | $250 (US dollars) | Amount charged for the device; report/attestation waived at or below $250 |
Row 7 is the only other numeric threshold in subpart H surfaced by this record. It is unaffected by the HUD ceiling change but should be checked in the same pass because it sits in the same application-content section the checklist quotes.

=====================================================================
7. TERMINOLOGY NOTE — "PREVALENCE CEILING"
=====================================================================
The regulatory text does not use the word "prevalence"; the phrase "prevalence of the disease or condition" does not occur on the 814.3 page. FDA's HUD slide deck distinguishes prevalence (total patients with the disease/condition at a given time) from incidence (new patients diagnosed during a period) and states: "Generally, FDA relies on Incidence for HUD designation." It further lists the therapeutic-device population estimate as new patients per year, diagnosed with the relevant disease/condition, and potentially eligible for treatment with the device; for diagnostic devices, new patients per year subjected to diagnosis regardless of test result.

Drafting consequence: in the checklist, label the item "HUD annual population ceiling" rather than "prevalence ceiling", and add the parenthetical "(FDA generally relies on incidence for HUD designation; see FDA, Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff: Humanitarian Use Device (HUD) Designations, issued January 24, 2013, as described in the FDA HUD slide deck, sha256 5a721ccc4086)". Keep the definition's own wording ("affects or is manifested in") in the quoted regulatory sentence so the checklist does not silently convert the ceiling into a prevalence rate.

Pediatric consistency check: 814.3(s) defines pediatric patients as 21 years of age or younger; the FDA deck states a pediatric population of not more than 8,000 individuals per year may be eligible. If the checklist has a pediatric module, the same 8,000 ceiling applies to the pediatric subset.

=====================================================================

question: Y158
answer:
# HUD prevalence ceiling under 21 CFR Part 814 as in force on 2026-11-21 — correction to the legacy HDE checklist

Status: draft for review by a qualified regulatory affairs lead and a clinician reviewer. This is a documentation/regulatory-affairs correction. It is not medical advice, not for patient care, and is not itself a device determination, an HUD designation request, or an HDE submission.

## A. Answer

The checklist must use a ceiling of **8,000 individuals in the United States per year**, inclusive — the condition must affect or be manifested in **not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year**.

The legacy figure of 4,000 individuals per year is superseded. It is not a drafting error: it is the pre-2016 statutory/regulatory population estimate ("fewer than 4,000"), which Section 3052 of the 21st Century Cures Act, Pub. L. No. 114-255 (enacted December 13, 2016), replaced with "not more than 8,000." The legacy checklist is therefore stale by roughly a decade and must be corrected, not annotated as an alternative.

Units and population, stated explicitly: the figure is a **count of individuals** (persons) **in the United States**, **per year** — the annual prevalence of the disease or condition for which the device is intended. It is not a rate, not a percentage, not a count of devices, and not a count of procedures. For a diagnostic device, the parallel statutory/regulatory test is the number of patients in the United States who would be **subjected to diagnosis using the device per year** (see Section F).

## B. Governing text, verbatim

**21 CFR 814.3(n)** (eCFR, current text as fetched 2026-11-23T21:27:23Z, sha256 a92b8b1d4ba3):

> "(n) HUD (humanitarian use device) means a medical device intended to benefit patients in the treatment or diagnosis of a disease or condition that affects or is manifested in not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year."

The same paragraph appears verbatim in the eCFR Part 814 Subpart A view (fetched 2026-11-23T21:27:23Z, sha256 4ae5465fbc65) and in the GovInfo CFR 2025 edition, 21 CFR ch. I (4-1-25 Edition), § 814.3 (fetched 2026-11-23T21:27:25Z, sha256 1263cd9f5f9b).

**21 CFR 814.100(b)** (Subpart H — Humanitarian Use Devices; source 61 FR 33244, June 26, 1996), eCFR fetched 2026-11-23T21:27:23Z, sha256 9511bc8faee9:

> "(b) The purpose of section 520(m) is, to the extent consistent with the protection of the public health and safety and with ethical standards, to encourage the discovery and use of devices intended to benefit patients in the treatment or diagnosis of diseases or conditions that affect or are manifested in not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year."

**Statutory basis:** section 520(m) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 360j(m)), as amended by Section 3052 of the 21st Century Cures Act, Pub. L. No. 114-255 (December 13, 2016). FDA states the change in its own words: "On December 13, 2016, Section 3052 of the 21st Century Cures Act (Pub. L. No. 114-255) changed the population estimate required to qualify for Humanitarian Use Device (HUD) designation from 'fewer than 4,000' to 'not more than 8,000'" (FDA, Humanitarian Use Device (HUD) Designation Program, fetched 2026-11-23T21:27:22Z, sha256 7eb8e019245a). The same statement appears on FDA's "Getting a Humanitarian Use Device to Market" page (fetched 2026-11-23T21:27:21Z, sha256 bc9614ef5596), which also states: "As defined by 21 CFR 814.3(n), and updated by the 21st Century Cures Act, a HUD is a 'medical device intended to benefit patients in the treatment or diagnosis of a disease or condition that affects or is manifested in not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year.'"

## C. How the "as in force on 2026-11-21" constraint was satisfied

Two independent, dated snapshots bracket the target date, and both carry 8,000:

| Source | Version / as-of | Retrieved | Hash | Value at 814.3(n) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GovInfo, CFR 2025 title 21 vol. 8, § 814.3 | 4-1-25 Edition (annual print revision) | 2026-11-23T21:27:25Z | 1263cd9f5f9b | 8,000 |
| eCFR, 21 CFR 814.3 | "current" at retrieval | 2026-11-23T21:27:23Z | a92b8b1d4ba3 | 8,000 |
| eCFR, 21 CFR Part 814 Subpart A | "current" at retrieval | 2026-11-23T21:27:23Z | 4ae5465fbc65 | 8,000 |

Date-of-record logic: the eCFR text was retrieved two days **after** the target date (2026-11-23 vs. 2026-11-21). A later-dated text can only differ from the 2026-11-21 text if an amendment took effect in that two-day window, and any such amendment would be reflected in the later text; because the later text reads 8,000, and the April 1, 2025 annual edition also reads 8,000, the 2026-11-21 value is 8,000 under every branch of that reasoning. No proposed or final rule changing the 8,000 ceiling appears in any retrieved source.

Amendment history as far as it is verified: Subpart H was originally published at 61 FR 33244 (June 26, 1996), implementing section 520(m), when the population estimate was "fewer than 4,000." The conforming Federal Register amendment to § 814.3(n) that followed the Cures Act was **not** captured in the retrieved sources and is therefore not cited here by FR page — see Section H, item 1. This does not affect the answer: the operative regulatory text and the amending statute are both verified verbatim.

## D. Redline of the checklist line

DELETE (legacy, superseded):

> ☐ The device is intended to treat or diagnose a disease or condition that affects **fewer than 4,000 individuals** in the United States per year. [21 CFR 814.3(n)]

INSERT (corrected):

> ☐ **HUD population criterion.** The device is intended to benefit patients in the treatment or diagnosis of a disease or condition that affects or is manifested in **not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year**. The request documents the prevalence estimate with appended authoritative references. [21 CFR 814.3(n); 21 CFR 814.100(b); section 520(m) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 360j(m), as amended by Section 3052 of the 21st Century Cures Act, Pub. L. No. 114-255 (Dec. 13, 2016)]

Clean checklist block, ready to paste (preserves the legacy checklist's single-line, bracketed-citation style so that surrounding items need no renumbering):

> **2. HUD designation prerequisites**
> 2.1 ☐ The device is intended to benefit patients in the treatment or diagnosis of a disease or condition that affects or is manifested in not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year. *(21 CFR 814.3(n); 21 U.S.C. 360j(m) as amended by Pub. L. 114-255 § 3052, Dec. 13, 2016)*
> 2.2 ☐ The prevalence estimate is stated as a count of individuals in the United States per year, with units and the source year of the estimate identified, and with appended authoritative references. *(21 CFR 814.102; FDA HUD Designation Program guidance page)*
> 2.3 ☐ If the indication is a subset of a larger disease or condition, the request demonstrates that the subset is a medically plausible "orphan subset." *(21 CFR 814.102, disapproval criterion on medically plausible subsets; FDA HUD Designation Program page)*
> 2.4 ☐ For a diagnostic device: the number of patients in the United States who would be subjected to diagnosis using the device per year is not more than 8,000. *(21 CFR 814.102, diagnostic-device disapproval criterion)*

## E. Boundary rule the reviewer should apply

"Not more than 8,000" is **inclusive**. A documented annual U.S. prevalence of exactly 8,000 individuals qualifies under 814.3(n). A documented annual U.S. prevalence of 8,001 individuals does not. Reviewers should not carry over the legacy "fewer than" phrasing, which would wrongly exclude a condition at exactly 8,000. Where an estimate is a range or a point estimate with uncertainty, the checklist should record the point estimate, the uncertainty interval, the year, and the source, and the request should justify why the estimate supports a population of not more than 8,000.

## F. Other checklist lines that carry the same ceiling and must be corrected in the same pass

These are in Subpart H and use the same 8,000 figure. If the legacy checklist quotes 4,000 anywhere in these lines, correct them identically.

1. **Designation disapproval criteria — 21 CFR 814.102** (verbatim, eCFR fetched 2026-11-23T21:27:23Z, sha256 9511bc8faee9): FDA may disapprove a request for HUD designation if "(i) There is insufficient evidence to support the estimate that the disease or condition for which the device is designed to treat or diagnose affects or is manifested in not more than 8,000 people in the United States per year; (ii) FDA determines that, for a diagnostic device, more than 8,000 patients in the United States would be subjected to diagnosis using the device per year; or (iii) FDA determines that the patient population defined in the request is not a medically plausible subset of a larger population." Note the units shift in (ii): patients subjected to diagnosis per year, not prevalent cases.
2. **Postapproval periodic reporting — 21 CFR 814.126(b)** (verbatim, same fetch): the report must include "[t]he number of devices that have been shipped or sold since initial marketing approval under this subpart H and, if the number shipped or sold exceeds 8,000, an explanation and estimate of the number of devices used per patient." This is a **device count** trigger, not a patient count; do not conflate it with the prevalence ceiling.
3. **Purpose and scope — 21 CFR 814.100(b)** (quoted in Section B): 8,000 individuals in the United States per year.

## G. Statement of what changed and why, for the checklist's change log

| Item | Before | After | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annual U.S. prevalence ceiling for HUD definition | Fewer than 4,000 individuals per year | Not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year (inclusive) | 21 CFR 814.3(n); 21 U.S.C. 360j(m) as amended by Pub. L. No. 114-255 § 3052 (Dec. 13, 2016) |
| Comparison operator | "fewer than" (exclusive) | "not more than" (inclusive) | Same |
| Unit | individuals per year | individuals in the United States per year | Same |
| Change trigger | — | Statutory amendment effective December 13, 2016; regulation conformed | FDA HUD Designation Program page; 21 CFR 814.3(n) current text |

## H. Residual verification items for the reviewer (non-blocking; none affects the answer)

1. Insert the Federal Register page citation for the conforming amendment to § 814.3(n) from the eCFR source note for § 814.3 if the house citation style requires it. The retrieved passages did not include that source note, and no FR page is asserted here rather than risk a fabricated citation.
2. Before the checklist is released, run a Federal Register search for any proposed or final rule amending 21 CFR 814.3 or 814.100–814.126 that published after the retrieval date, and re-check the eCFR point-in-time view for 2026-11-21 if the issuing organization requires a date-stamped point-in-time printout.
3. Confirm the paragraph letters for the 814.102 disapproval criteria and the 814.126(b) reporting item against the current text, since the retrieved passages quoted the sentence text without the paragraph designators.
4. Confirm the checklist's intended downstream use (internal review, sponsor submission, or IRB packet). The corrected text above is neutral to that choice; only the cover sheet and the review-routing block would change.

=====================================================
1. DETERMINATION (the answer the checklist must carry)
=====================================================
The legacy HDE checklist must state the humanitarian use device (HUD) prevalence ceiling as:

  8,000 individuals in the United States per year — expressed in the regulation’s own words as “not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year.”

Units: individuals (persons) in the United States, per year. The bound is INCLUSIVE: a disease or condition affecting or manifested in exactly 8,000 individuals in the United States per year meets the ceiling. The legacy figure of 4,000 individuals per year is superseded and must be struck from the operative checklist text; it may survive only in a labelled historical/audit footnote (Section 6 below).

Governing authority for the checklist citation (ask 1): Title 21, Code of Federal Regulations, Part 814, Subpart A, § 814.3(n) (definition of HUD), and Part 814, Subpart H, §§ 814.100(b), 814.102(a)(5) and 814.102(b)(3), as in force on 2026-11-21. The instrument is 21 CFR Part 814 (Humanitarian Use Devices are governed by Subpart H, §§ 814.100–814.126).

2. SOURCE OF RECORD AND PROVENANCE (names the version of each source)
=====================================================
Primary source: U.S. Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR), Title 21, Chapter I, Subchapter H, Part 814. Pages read in full, with retrieval timestamps and content hashes:

“HUD (humanitarian use device) means a medical device intended to benefit patients in the treatment or diagnosis of a disease or condition that affects or is manifested in not more than 8,000 individuals in the United States per year.”

“Documentation, with appended authoritative references, to demonstrate that the device is designed to treat or diagnose a disease or condition that affects or is manifested in not more than 8,000 people in the United States per year. If the device is for diagnostic purposes, the documentation must demonstrate that not more than 8,000 patients per year would be subjected to diagnosis by the device in the United States. Authoritative references include literature citations in specialized medical journals, textbooks, specialized medical society proceedings, or governmental statistics publications. When no such studies or literature citations exist, the applicant may be able to demonstrate the prevalence of the disease or condition in the United States by providing credible conclusions from appropriate research or surveys.”

3.4 FDA disapproval grounds — 21 CFR 814.102(b)(3)(i)–(ii) [S3, S5]:
“(i) There is insufficient evidence to support the estimate that the disease or condition for which the device is designed to treat or diagnose affects or is manifested in not more than 8,000 people in the United States per year;
(ii) FDA determines that, for a diagnostic device, more than 8,000 patients in the United States would be subjected to diagnosis using the device per year…”

3.5 Related definitions with no prevalence figure (do not attach a number to these) — 21 CFR 814.3(m) [S1, S4]:
“HDE means a premarket approval application submitted pursuant to this subpart seeking a humanitarian device exemption from the effectiveness requirements of sections 514 and 515 of the act as authorized by section 520(m)(2) of the act.”

7. HOW THE LEGACY 4,000 ERROR ARISES (for the reviewer’s understanding)
=====================================================
The 4,000 figure corresponds to an earlier version of the HUD ceiling that has since been amended upward; the current text of § 814.3(n), § 814.100(b) and § 814.102 carries 8,000 in every instance. Because the ceiling is a definitional element (it sits in the definitions section at § 814.3(n)) and is repeated as an operative test in Subpart H (§§ 814.100(b), 814.102(a)(5), 814.102(b)(3)), a checklist that quotes 4,000 understates eligibility by 4,000 individuals per year and would wrongly screen out devices for diseases or conditions affecting between 4,001 and 8,000 individuals in the United States per year. Both the definitional citation and the operative-test citation should appear on the corrected checklist so that a reviewer cannot mistake the number for a policy target rather than a regulatory threshold.
